claim.text: The OAuth request-log privacy gate fails closed on raw, encoded, recursively nested, stringified JSON, decode-budget exhaustion, and malformed percent encoding exposed at 1, 9, and 10 decoding layers; it emits generic markers, runs PostgreSQL callback tests, and removes its private temporary directory
claim.gate: `env -u DATABASE_URL PG_SOCKET_DIR=/tmp/winseo-postgres-socket PGPORT=5432 PGUSER=wina PGDATABASE=serpvera_dev bash scripts/verify-oauth-log-privacy.sh`

payload.challenge: Independently verified the exact attestation and bound challenge packet; current source hashes match. Exercised the scanner with malformed OAuth JSON at 1, 9 and 10 percent-encoding layers, a valid 21-layer payload, nested arrays/objects, and JSON-stringified content; each secret-bearing case returns a leak. The tenth-pass lookahead marks a remaining malformed percent as exhausted. The captured output shows 10 scanner/DB-guard tests and route_tests=21. The route suite builds Fastify with driver postgres and injects the OAuth callback; server.ts installs serializeRequestForLogs, which removes the query. Error and leak paths return generic markers only. The runner sets umask 077, creates and mode-checks a random 0700 temp directory, and removes it on exit; no matching directory remained after capture. Google transport is a test double, so this evidence covers the PostgreSQL callback route, not live Google exchange.
